----Petitioner

For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Umesh Kant Vyas.
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sharwan Singh Rathore, Pp.
 Ms. Jaya Bhati, for the complainant.
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajendra Prakash Soni
Order 08/10/2024

1 .  This is an anticipatory bail moved on behalf of the applicant in relation to F.I.R. No. 11/2021 of Police Station Rani, District Pali, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465,
467, 468, 471, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Learned counsel representing the petitioner vehemently urged that petitioner is innocent person and present FIR filed against the petitioner is false and baseless; that the petitioner is apprehending his arrest in a false case; that there is no record to show as to how ingredients of offences under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC are made out against him besides other offences; that his custodial interrogation is not required; that there are no allegations of petitioner tampering with the evidence and nothing is to be recovered from applicant.
[CRLMB-8453/2024] Therefore, to protect his life and liberty an order of anticipatory bail may be passed in his favour.

3. From the other side, learned Public Prosecutor for the State has strongly objected the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant and submitted that on the basis of material collected so Naresh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:41055) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58082328/
1 far, the investigation officer has reason to believe that petitioner is guilty of offences alleged by the complainant.

Highlighting the non-cooperation in investigation by petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently submitted that in the absence of custodial interrogation of petitioner,
investigation in this case cannot be taken to its logical conclusion in view of nature of gravity of offence.
He thus, prayed that in the facts of the present case, it is expedient that anticipatory bail application be dismissed.
4. I have appreciated the submissions advanced by the learned defence counsel and learned Public Prosecutor and have carefully perused the material available on record.

5. Applying the dictum and parameters to the instant case as laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth vs State Of Gujarat reported in (2016) 1 SCC 152 and after having heard both the sides at length and on perusal of the Case-diary as well as material on record, it appears prima facie that at this stage of the investigation, the main question in this case is whether the disputed lease was signed by the petitioner in his capacity as Sarpanch or whether the leaseholder forged the Sarpanch's signature. In such a case of cheating and forgery, where the investigation is primarily based on [2024:RJ-JD:41055] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-8453/2024] documentary evidence of the Gram Panchayat, Bhadarlau, the Court is of the opinion that there is no need for the custodial interrogation of the petitioner.

entities.text: Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth vs State Of Gujarat reported in (2016) 1 SCC 152
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the investigation relies on documents or records,
which are already available, the necessity for custodial interrogation is eliminated.

6. As an upshot of the above discussion and having regard to the overall facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioner under Section 438 Cr. P.C.
7. Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest of petitioner Naresh S/o Bhanwarlal in connection with the FIR No. 11/2021, Police Station Rani, District Pali, the petitioner shall be released on bail; provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- along with two sureties of Rs. 25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer/SHO on the following conditions: -
(i) that the petitioner shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) that the petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or any police officer;
(iii) that the petitioner shall not leave India without [2024:RJ-JD:41055] (4 of 4)
[CRLMB-8453/2024] previous permission of the court.
(iv) that the petitioners shall abide by all the conditions specified under section 438(2) Cr.P.C. and shall appear before the investigating officer as and when called for.

9. Disposed of accordingly.
